tldr: OpenAI's product lead traced ChatGPT Work's growth from Codex's 0-to-10M-user run to a full agentic assistant (Sites, Memory, Subagents, Finance, no-code) on Jul 28. An outside engineering write-up followed on Aug 4, reconstructing how Memory, Proactivity, Scheduling, Browser Use, Plugins, Skills, and Tools actually fit together inside the product.
whats_new: OpenAI shipped an improved GPT-5.6 Sol inside ChatGPT on Aug 6 and widened free-tier access to GPT-5.6 Luna, extending the same push toward broader, cheaper access that ChatGPT Work has been built around.
why_it_matters: The Aug 4 reconstruction is the closest public look yet at how OpenAI composes Memory, Scheduling, Browser Use, and Skills into one agent product — a reference architecture worth comparing against your own agent stack.

beats.headline: OpenAI traces ChatGPT Work's roots to Codex's 0-to-10M-user growth
beats.summary: Product lead Akshay Nathan walks through how Codex's early adoption shaped ChatGPT Work's build-out of Sites, Memory, Subagents, Finance, and no-code tools.

beats.headline: Outside engineers reconstruct how Memory, Scheduling, Browser Use, Skills, and Tools fit together
beats.summary: An independent write-up pieces together the internals OpenAI hadn't detailed publicly, framing ChatGPT Work as "the agent for a billion users."

beats.headline: GPT-5.6 Sol improves and GPT-5.6 Luna free access widens

open_questions: Does OpenAI publish an official architecture breakdown of ChatGPT Work's Memory/Scheduling/Browser-Use stack, or does the outside reconstruction stay the best public reference?
Does the wider GPT-5.6 Luna free tier carry the same agent capabilities (Memory, Subagents, Tools) as the paid ChatGPT Work tier, or is it a lighter separate product?
take_for_builders: Compare the reconstructed ChatGPT Work stack (Memory, Scheduling, Browser Use, Skills, Tools) against your own agent architecture before building the same primitives from scratch.
